questions.question: Define the primary, secondary and tertiary sectors and give two South African examples of businesses in each.
questions.expected_answer: Primary: extracts or harvests natural resources (e.g. a maize farm, a platinum mine, a hake fishing company, a forestry plantation). Secondary: processes raw materials into goods, manufactures and constructs (e.g. a maize mill, a vehicle assembly plant, a construction company, an Eskom power station). Tertiary: provides services and distributes goods (e.g. a supermarket, a bank, a minibus taxi, a hotel, a school or hospital).

questions.question: Classify each and give a reason: (a) a bakery that bakes bread; (b) a supermarket that resells bread; (c) a coal-fired power station; (d) a gold mine.
questions.expected_answer: (a) Secondary: it manufactures bread from ingredients. (b) Tertiary: it sells goods it did not make (a service). (c) Secondary: it produces electricity, a physical product. (d) Primary: it extracts minerals from the earth.

questions.question: Explain why the tertiary sector is the largest in South Africa and why the primary sector remains important.
questions.expected_answer: As incomes rise, people spend a growing share on services (finance, health, education, tourism, communication), and businesses need more services; productivity gains in farming and manufacturing mean fewer workers are needed there. The tertiary sector produces roughly two-thirds of GDP. The primary sector remains important because mining and agriculture earn a large share of export income, supply raw materials for the secondary sector and provide jobs in rural areas.
